panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A1, A2, B1, B2). A1: Frontal clinical photograph of the 6-month-old patient with cat-eye syndrome (article title and caption) showing the captioned craniofacial dysmorphism: hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures and malformed external ears/preauricular tags. Additional described features (thin upper lip, retrognathism) are not in the vocabulary. A2: Profile clinical photograph of the same 6-month-old patient with cat-eye syndrome, showing the malformed external ear and craniofacial dysmorphism described in the caption. B1: Frontal clinical photograph of the same patient at 3.5 years with cat-eye syndrome, showing the captioned facial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures, ear malformation). B2: Profile clinical photograph of the same patient at 3.5 years with cat-eye syndrome, showing the malformed external ear and craniofacial dysmorphism described in the caption.

panels.figure_caption: Craniofacial dysmorphism. Pictures of the patient at the age of 6 months (top panel) and 3 and a half (bottom panel). The facial dysmorphism consisted in hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures, a thin upper lip, retrognathism, an irregularly shaped skull, and severe malformation of the external ears.
in_text_mentions: 38 weeks of gestation, with a birth weight of 2800 g (10th percentile) and a head circumference of 35 cm (50–75th percentile). A clinical examination revealed an imperforate anus, facial dysmorphism (Figure 1), general hypotonia, and bilateral malformation of the external ears (present as several tags, in combination with atresia of the external auditory canal) (Figure 1). Hearing tests evidenced a 70 dB bilateral conductive hearing loss. A CT scan showed bilateral hypoplasia of the tympanic cavity and right-side hypoplasia of the middle ear. panels.stated_ethnicity_quote: Cat Eye Syndrome in a Sudanese Infant
panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of a 5-month-old infant with caption-confirmed Cat Eye Syndrome showing preauricular skin tags and left microtia; facial features including hypertelorism are described in-text. Article title and caption both attribute findings directly to Cat Eye Syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Khalid and Fadl‐Elmula. Cat Eye Syndrome in a Sudanese Infant: Congenital Cataract in the Absence of Iris Coloboma: A Case Report.. Clinical case reports 2026. doi:10.1002/ccr3.72922. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical features of Cat Eye Syndrome in a 5‐month‐old female infant. Facial asymmetry with left microtia, multiple preauricular skin tags, left eye congenital cataract.
in_text_mentions: vealed multisystem involvement. Craniofacial dysmorphic features included microcephaly, epicanthal folds, hypertelorism, a depressed nasal bridge, and a long philtrum. Ocular examination revealed a left‐sided lenticular opacity consistent with congenital cataract; notably, no iris coloboma was observed. Auricular findings comprised complete agenesis of the left external ear (microtia) with multiple preauricular skin tags and low‐set contralateral ear positioning. Neck and trunk examination demonstrated a short neck and widely spaced nipples. Limb examination revealed clenched hands (Figure 1).
